company.name: Rownd
company.shortDescription: Rownd is a B2B SaaS frictionless authentication company.
company.description: Rownd helps companies align the friction of authentication with the rewards of their apps.  Rownd customers can decide how and where authentication happens across their website, blog, landing pages, webapps, and mobile apps.

productsAndServices.description: Provides secure, frictionless user authentication using passkeys and magic links without requiring passwords.

productsAndServices.description: Enables tailoring of sign-in, subscription, and user management flows to align with specific branding and user experience needs.
productsAndServices.name: Customizable User Flows

productsAndServices.description: Provides software development kits and APIs to integrate authentication, payments, and deep linking quickly into apps.

productsAndServices.description: Delivers smart deep links that direct users to specific app locations across devices, enhancing navigation and marketing campaigns.

insights.title: Valuation increased across disclosed rounds
insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $1,167,716 to $16,516,464, a 14.14x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.

insights.title: Sharp recent attention and growth momentum
insights.statement: Crunchbase scores growth at 59 (+0 over 90 days) and market heat at 63 (-3).
insights.implication: The company has recently become much more visible, but the scores should be treated as attention/activity indicators rather than revenue or clinical-performance metrics.
caveats: Crunchbase does not expose the complete weighting behind these proprietary scores.

insights.title: Competitive benchmark reflects the modeled peer set
insights.statement: Crunchbase’s closest modeled peers include Stytch, Clerk, Auth0.
insights.implication: These matches provide a starting point for comparing differentiation, scale, and shared specialties, but they should not be treated as a verified competitor set.
caveats: Similarity scores are algorithmic matches, not verified direct competitors.
